text:
Forensic findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork under a uniform docket number, assigns each artifact a creation date and an owning account, and routes documents between custodians through named channels. Retention is tiered: working files persist in an active folder, completed items move to an archive after a closing date, and audit logs record every access, edit, and transfer with a timestamp and actor identifier. Periodic audits compare docket fields against custody chains to verify that each document's metadata matches its filing history. No substantive content is evaluated; the office verifies structure, sequence, and authorization.

2) What occurred: The actor opened a docket under a named account and filed a series of dated intake forms. Each form carried a donor-identifier field, a debt-schedule field, and a consent-attestation field. The actor populated the debt-schedule field with values sourced from a creditor ledger, then entered a pressure-narrative field describing inducement language. Consent-attestation fields were completed with a signature block, a date, and a witness line; in three records the signature block was filled in without a corresponding identity-verification artifact in the same folder. The actor then created routing memoranda in a transfer channel, each naming a recipient account, a destination-clinic code, and a routing date. The memoranda were filed out of sequence relative to the intake forms, with two routing memoranda dated before the associated consent-attestation fields were completed. The actor edited two medical-clearance documents, overwriting a condition field with a cleared status, and re-dated the clearance field to precede the original examination date. A compliance-review field in each docket was left blank; no authority-notification artifact appears in the folder. The docket was closed with a completion date and moved to the archive, and the audit log shows the actor accessed the archived docket once, after the closing date, and exported the folder to an external account.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor held a named administrative account with edit rights on intake forms, routing memoranda, and medical-clearance documents, and with archive-access rights on closed dockets. The routing channel in use was a named internal transfer queue with no secondary-approval field. The external account used for export was a personal mail account not registered in the docket's custody list. The creditor ledger referenced in the debt-schedule field was a spreadsheet file attached to the docket; no retention policy artifact references it. The witness line on the consent-attestation forms references an employee ID not present in the staff roster attached to the docket.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Docket field inconsistencies: a consent-attestation field dated after the associated routing memorandum; two medical-clearance documents with an edited condition field and a re-dated clearance field; a routing memorandum referencing a recipient account that has no intake form in the same docket. Channel anomalies: routing memoranda filed directly to the transfer queue without a supervisor-approval field populated; an export event in the audit log originating from an archived docket, destined for an account outside the custody list. Metadata anomalies: file-modification timestamps on the edited clearances later than the stated document dates; a spreadsheet attachment with no originating system metadata. The closing date on the docket post-dates the last recorded field edit by one day, and no compliance-review artifact was ever created.
